name: Ghana
headline: Ghana: +6.0% growth in 2025, 14.2% inflation, debt 49% of GDP
sections: Ghana is a $115 billion economy (2025), the world's 71st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.0% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $8,610 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 10.1% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 14.2% in 2025, well above typical central bank targets, down from 31.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 5.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 49% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 79% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.3% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +8.1% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 69% of GDP (2024), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.7% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 47% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 65.7 years (2024). Population: 35.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
